passages.text: CALORIC, the name given by the French chemists to the matter of heat, a subtle fluid which pervades all bodies, and the accumulation of which produces the sensation of warmth.
It flows from hotter bodies into colder, until both are of one temperature.
When caloric enters a body it separates its particles, and so causes it to expand; and when enough is added, solids are melted and liquids turned into vapour.
In melting ice and boiling water a great quantity of caloric disappears without raising the heat; this Dr Black called latent heat.
Count Rumford, observing the great heat produced in boring cannon, concluded that heat is not a substance but a motion of the particles of bodies; but his opinion has found few followers.
Caloric is supposed to have no sensible weight, since a body weighs the same hot or cold.
The caloric theory is an obsolete theory that heat consists of a self-repellent fluid called caloric that flows from hotter bodies to colder bodies. Antoine Lavoisier named it in the 1780s.
Heat flows from a hotter body to a colder one until they reach the same temperature, an observation the caloric theory explained well.
Heating makes the particles of a substance move faster and further apart, so most materials expand; with enough heat, solids melt and liquids boil.
Joseph Black found that melting and boiling absorb heat without changing the temperature, and called this latent heat. The term is still used.
In 1798 Count Rumford measured the heat produced by boring cannon and argued that friction could produce heat without limit, which a conserved fluid could not explain.
In the 1840s James Joule showed that work can be converted into heat at a fixed rate. Heat is now understood as energy transferred because of a temperature difference, and caloric was abandoned.
Caloric was thought to be weightless, which fitted the observation that bodies weigh the same hot or cold.

reasons: Same headword: CALORIC and Caloric theory.
Rare terms appear in both: latent heat, Black, Rumford, boring cannon.
Heat scores well but describes the modern view, so it is a second candidate.

alignments.label: Heat as a fluid

britannica.quote: a subtle fluid which pervades all bodies

wikipedia.quote: Heat is now understood as energy transferred

alignments.note: There is no heat fluid. Heat is energy in transit.

alignments.label: Hot to cold

britannica.quote: It flows from hotter bodies into colder, until both are of one temperature

wikipedia.quote: Heat flows from a hotter body to a colder one until they reach the same temperature

alignments.note: The observation holds, whatever heat is.

alignments.label: Expansion

britannica.quote: it separates its particles, and so causes it to expand

wikipedia.quote: move faster and further apart, so most materials expand

alignments.note: Particles move apart in both accounts. Only the reason changed.

alignments.label: Latent heat

britannica.quote: this Dr Black called latent heat

wikipedia.quote: called this latent heat. The term is still used

alignments.note: A term from the caloric era that survived the theory.

britannica.quote: observing the great heat produced in boring cannon

wikipedia.quote: measured the heat produced by boring cannon

alignments.label: Few followers

britannica.quote: his opinion has found few followers

alignments.note: True in 1817, no longer: Rumford's view won by the 1850s.

alignments.label: No weight

britannica.quote: a body weighs the same hot or cold

wikipedia.quote: bodies weigh the same hot or cold

alignments.note: The observation holds. It now shows heat is not a substance at all.

suggestedQuestions: Which ideas from the caloric theory are still used?

Was Rumford right about heat?.answer: Yes. The 1817 entry reports that Rumford concluded from boring cannon that heat is a motion of particles, but says his view found few followers [B5]. Wikipedia says Rumford argued that friction could make heat without limit, and that Joule's work in the 1840s led to heat being understood as energy [W5] [W6].

Which ideas from the caloric theory are.answer: The observations, and one term. Heat still flows from hot to cold until temperatures are equal [B2] [W2], and Black's term latent heat is still used [B4] [W4]. The idea of heat as a fluid is not [W6].
